STEP 3b: confirmed this table is the 3D-WS block and not the sibling ASTI table -- the live items are Cog_1..4/Refl_1..4/Aff_1..4 (12 items, three four-item facets), matching the 3D-WS-12; the ASTI block is the deposit's separate ST_1..ST_7 columns. The live codes correspond to the full abbreviated scale, not a subset. MAPPING (reconstructed): the IRW codes are the OSF deposit's own column names (data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py melts them through unchanged), but the deposit is a bare CSV with no variable labels, so the codes give the facet and a within-facet position and nothing else. The shipped order is each facet in parent-3D-WS item-number order (Cog_1=c9, Cog_2=c10, Cog_3=c11, Cog_4=c13; Refl_1=r8r, Refl_2=r9, Refl_3=r10, Refl_4=r12; Aff_1=a4r, Aff_2=a7r, Aff_3=a9, Aff_4=a12). The rival ordering -- the 3D-WS-12 questionnaire's own 1..12 order -- is REFUTED by the data: it would make Refl_1 the negatively-worded r10, and Refl_1 is one of the three items the authors' own scoring enters unreversed. See verify_pellerin2020_3dws.R (VERDICT: PASS) and verification_pellerin2020_3dws.csv; Step 5b status is PARTIAL -- the affective within-pair order (a4r vs a7r, a9 vs a12) and the whole cognitive within-facet order are order inference that no route separates. TEXT (translated_substitute): the study administered the scale in French. The French wording is in neither the OSF deposit (only two files, PsyR_lockdown2020.R and data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv; the CSV has bare column codes and no variable labels, the R file is analysis-only) nor the Frontiers article, which has no supplementary material and reproduces only three example items, in English. Ardelt's page distributes the French translation by email request only, which this pipeline does not do, so the documented English fallback applies: official English in the base fields, _translated columns omitted, language=French. OPTIONS: the paper states all resources were measured on a Likert scale from 1 = 'strongly disagree' to 7 = 'strongly agree'; only those two endpoints are labelled and scale points 2-6 were left blank, not padded. Note this is NOT the 3D-WS-12's own anchor set (1 = 'definitely true of myself' .. 5 = 'not true of myself'), so the instrument's own instruction line ('How much are the following statements true of yourself?') would misdescribe what these respondents saw and `instructions` is deliberately left blank rather than borrowed. RIGHTS: the 3D-WS/3D-WS-12 is a named published instrument (Ardelt 2003; Thomas et al. 2017), so the deposit's CC BY licence does not govern the wording. instrument_rights_register.csv carries no row for it. Ardelt's own page (people.clas.ufl.edu/ardelt/home/the-three-dimensional-wisdom-scale-3d-ws, sha256 22cf018e9046a56c579b50ddf1faf42e1fa719eaeb0a798d8f8412939fe365c4, fetched 2026-09-20) publishes the complete 12-item and 39-item questionnaires as free PDFs and states no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term. Its only contact sentence is 'Please contact Dr. Monika Ardelt at ardelt@ufl.edu to obtain an MS Word file of the 3D-WS, the 3D-WS-12, or a specific translation of the 3D-WS.' -- an offer to supply a file format and a translation, not a condition on using the wording she already publishes. No reserved right locatable or quotable, so not blocked. No register row written: a round may write a block row but never a ship row. DATA CAVEAT: the authors' own derived wisdom score (the deposit's P.Wisdom column) is the mean of only 11 of the 12 columns -- Cog_1 is dropped -- and Cog_1 is anomalous in the live table, correlating -0.21 to -0.23 with the three reflective items once every item is keyed in the authors' own direction. The IRW table carries all 12 columns, Cog_1 included.
public_note: Item text for pellerin2020_3dws is the 3D-WS-12's published English wording; the study administered the scale in French and no French version of the items appears in its OSF deposit or its article, so what is shown here is a parallel English version rather than the sentences respondents read. Within each facet the item-to-code order is inferred: the reflective block is verified against the instrument's published loadings and freed residual, and the three positively-worded items land exactly where the authors' own scoring key says they do, but Cog_1-Cog_4 could be any of the 24 orders of c9/c10/c11/c13 as far as the data can tell. Separately, the authors' own wisdom score excludes Cog_1, whose responses correlate negatively with the reflective items once keyed in the same direction as its facet-mates (r = -0.21, -0.21, -0.21 against Refl_2/Refl_3/Refl_4 at wave 0, n=674, the wave the authors' own score is computed on; -0.21 to -0.23 pooling all 1010 person-wave records); the IRW table keeps it.

DEVIATION TO DISCLOSE: option_text ships in ENGLISH while item_text is Arabic. The deposit never publishes the Arabic anchor labels - codebook.csv gives the scale only as the English coding string '5=strongly agree,4=agree,3=neutral,2=disagree,1=strongly disagree (blank=missing)', the data file stores bare integers, and the deposit has exactly two files and no associated article - so the administered Arabic anchors are not recoverable within the deposit's scope. Rather than invent Arabic, the English anchors sit in option_text with option_text_translated blank. instructions and section_prompt are blank: no administered instruction text is published anywhere in the deposit (the Mendeley record's prose description describes the study, not wording anyone read). correct_response is blank throughout - attitude/self-rating scale, no key. section_id is a single trivial ramadan_2026_perceived_competence_1 with blank section_prompt; no testlet/passage structure. STEP 3B: the live item set is exactly the codebook's dimension-3 block, tagged '3 Prompt Engineering & Critical Appraisal', while the IRW table is named perceived_competence; the instrument field follows the codebook. PC1-PC4 are self-rated capability statements ('I can write prompts...', 'I verify the references AI cites...') and PC5-PC6 are negatively worded difficulty statements ('I experience weakness in accurate Arabic content...'), so 'perceived competence' is a fair but loose paraphrase of the dimension - an IRW dictionary/naming question, not an itemtext defect.
